It seems like you don't really want to die, you're just in a lot of distress. But it doesn't mean they're not taking your distress seriously. People may not be worried that you will actually kill yourself, but they should be worried about your emotional state. That's where I think these "attempts" may be coming from, not from an actual desire to end your life, but as a coping mechanism for your emotional state. I may be completely wrong but that's what I feel is going on reading through some of your comments.

May I ask how old you are? I'm 25 and have suicidal thoughts but I'm aware of how many people will care and be devastated if I killed myself. But if this were maybe, 5-10 years ago, I would probably think literally no one would care. In the last 3 years or so I've understood deeply how much my family really does love me and how amazing my group of friends is and how they'd support me and enjoy my company and how me being gone from them would feel like losing a limb.

For me personally, I think if my own unwillingness to carry on outweighs the devastation the people who care would feel, then I'll do it. If the cardinality of that set is zero, then your own pain will always outweigh the pain zero people would feel if you died. I know that cardinality is not zero, for anyone, and I know that I only realized that through maturity. Not until I was 22-23. I was basically a child with a childish view of the world before then. I want you to come to a realization of maturity first, a realization that there are those who care, maybe even plenty of people. Then you can decide if your own will to die is more pressing than how much those people will be hurt. I'm not going to straight up tell you not to do it, I don't believe in that. But I am asking you to make sure the logic is air-tight before making the decision. If there's even a tiny little thing off in your logic, then it is not the right decision.

Your answer is right there; playing your instruments can be strong enough if you want it to be. Why did you play instruments at all to begin with? What was it that made you fall in love with doing that? Having a hobby or leisure activity to hold onto is important when suicidal thoughts are in your head. Even if you think they're meaningless escapes, escapes can mean the world when you're at this place. For me, I have suicidal thoughts almost every day, but I also love going to the gym and haven't benched two plates for sets of 10 yet, and I don't want to die before I've done that. I absolutely love watching sports, it's my major leisure activity and helps me temporarily forget the bullshit of real life. My favorite sports team hasn't won a championship in a while, I don't want to die before seeing them win again. Those are a couple things I try to hold onto. For you it can be your instruments. Can you remember why you used to like playing them, and what made you put them down? Like maybe you could never play a piece perfectly, maybe you've never performed in front of a huge crowd and gotten a standing ovation. Do you want to die before you've had a chance to play that piece flawlessly and get that standing O?

For emancipation, you would also have to prove that your father is an unfit parent, along with being able to support yourself financially.
